narrative.overview:
**Creative North Star: "The Darkroom Wall"**

The photographs are the room's only color and its only spectacle. Everything else is the wall they hang on: a near-neutral ground, hairlines instead of boxes, and type in two registers. Titles shout once in Inter Tight Black, set tight; everything else speaks in small IBM Plex Mono. The interface is a quiet frame for reaching an inquiry or a booking.

Dark is the default and light is a second world, each tuned on its own terms and never inverted. The theme follows the visitor's system, and the half-disc toggle overrides it for the session. Type and scrims laid over a photograph stay light in both themes.

V3 is square. UI corners are 0, photographs take 4px, the About portrait 8px, and the only pill is the filter chip. Motion is a few authored moments (the hero crossfade, the logo strip drift, the glass header arriving), all off under reduced motion. Several pre-V3 surfaces still ship (the discipline strips with their rail, the commission booking card at /book/<commission>, the contact plate); they keep their own corners and are described under Components so they are not mistaken for drift.

**Motion tokens** (app/styles/tokens.css on origin/next): three curves only. `out` is `--ease-out-strong` (enter, leave, answer a click), `move` is `--ease-in-out-strong` (something travelling), `drawer` is `--ease-drawer` (page and sheet slides, line 84). No ease-in. Six durations, each with one job (lines 236 to 241): press 100ms, hover 150ms, small 250ms (menus, notices, chips, every exit), page 400ms, photo 600ms (a photo travelling), show 1000ms (splash and hero crossfade only). An exit takes about two thirds of its entrance. `--ease-rubber` (line 115) is only for a strip's release past an end. Values are in the sidecar's `extensions.motion`.
keyCharacteristics: Two faces only: Inter Tight 900 for the name and every title, IBM Plex Mono for everything else. The V4 hero tagline in Geist Mono is the one exception.
The name is always one line, "Julian Gigola" in title case.
Small text is uppercase mono at 0.14em; prose is sentence case.
Square UI. Filled means primary, one filled button per view.
One chromatic accent (teal), for focus, the current step and the picked option. Never decoration.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Teal marks focus, the current step and the picked option, never a fill, a status or decoration.

rules.name: The Tuned Twins Rule
rules.body: A color added to one theme is added to the other, re-set for that ground's contrast, not mirrored.

rules.name: The Photo Is Always Night Rule
rules.body: Anything laid on a photograph uses the on-photo set and the scrim, whatever the theme. Two exceptions ship. The V4 hero name and its tagline take the theme's own ink, no shadow, on a band of the page color along the foot of the hero, in both themes (.mt-name); the bands are the lightest that keep the name at 4.5:1. The home header under its frost takes the theme's ink too: the frost is a 62% veil of the page color, so dark ink in light and light ink in dark hold at least 6:1 over any photo, and every word shares it.

rules.name: The Two Registers Rule
rules.body: Type either shouts (Inter Tight 900, tight, large) or whispers (small mono). No third family, no weight in between. One exception ships: the V4 hero tagline in Geist Mono 600. It is a mono, so it stays in the whisper register.

rules.name: The One Line Name Rule
rules.body: "Julian Gigola" sits on one line wherever it appears. Size it down before letting it wrap.

rules.name: The Fit the Line Rule
rules.body: A name that must hold one line is fitted between a documented floor and ceiling, never wrapped or truncated.

rules.name: The Flat Plate Rule
rules.body: No drop shadows under content, no inner shine, no glow. One exception ships: the home film numbers carry a tight dark halo (stacked text-shadows from 2px to 10px) with no plate or patch behind them, so they read on the palest frame.

rules.name: The Pill Means Filter Rule
rules.body: In V3 a pill is a filter chip and nothing else. Buttons are square.

rules.name: The Fail Open Rule
rules.body: Content is visible by default. A block hides for its reveal only after the observer has seen it, so a failed observer, a crawler or an old WebView still shows everything.

rules.name: The 200% Zoom Rule
rules.body: Under max-width: 299.98px (a phone at 200% zoom) rows wrap, grids drop to one column (the home masonry to two), long lines wrap and nothing truncates or leaves the screen. No link hides by width or pointer alone; only a decorative label may (the footer's San Jose label). Legal shows at every width.

dos: Do let the photograph carry the color; keep chrome within chroma 0.005 except the teal accent and the two statuses.
Do set every title in Inter Tight 900 at -0.05em on a role from the ramp, and keep the name on one line.
Do use the label style (11px mono, 0.14em, uppercase) for small text, numbers in tabular figures.
Do keep one filled button per view; pair it with outline buttons.
Do use the on-photo set and the scrim for anything on a photograph, in both themes.
Do design each new surface in both themes before calling it done.
Do keep content visible by default; hide a block for its reveal only after the observer has seen it.
Do use the JG monogram from `logo/kit/` wherever a mark is needed.
donts: Don't use a pill for anything but a filter chip in V3.
Don't use glow, neon, gradients as decoration, or shadows under cards.

Don't put a decorative eyebrow or kicker above a title; only the audience lines over the doors and the service-page keyword line stay. They are not decoration (Julian, 2026-11-11): the audience line over each door ("For art directors and artists", "For private clients", "Published and commissioned by" over the client strip), and the keyword line over a service page's h1 (`kicker` in `lib/booking/booking.ts`, it carries search terms).
Don't add a third type family or a weight between the 900 titles and the mono. The V4 hero tagline's Geist Mono 600 is the one exception.
Don't use the teal accent as a fill or for status.
Don't make logos react to hover.
Don't outline a surface to lift it; step its lightness instead.
Don't hide a link by width or pointer; only a decorative label may hide.
Don't hide content until a script shows it.
standingChecks: Text holds 4.5:1 over photos in both themes, header words included (large display text 3:1). The header reports each word's worst contrast in `data-cr`.
At 200% zoom on a phone (300px wide) nothing is cut off, hidden or scrolls sideways.
With scroll observers off, every block is visible.
Both themes and reduced motion pass before a surface is done.
direction: Palette, 60/30/10: 60 ground (Warm Charcoal / Cold Paper), 30 photography, 10 ink and hairlines. Teal stays under 1%, for focus and the current step only.
Type: Inter Tight 900 shouts, IBM Plex Mono whispers. Geist Mono for the hero tagline only.
Layout: full bleed, held stages on the home, square UI.
References: to pick, 3 to 5 of Julian's own frames.
Never: glow, neon, decorative gradients, shadows under cards, a second accent, the eye mark.
Standing checks: see Do's and Don'ts.
